videos.title: This River runs across 4 Countries?! 🤯
videos.description:
Why does the Danube flow through 4 capital cities, and where does part of it disappear? The Danube Sinkhole at Immendingen, Germany, on a 3D map.

The Danube runs through Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade, more capitals than any other river, and touches 10 countries on its way to the Black Sea. Vienna and Bratislava are only about 56 km apart. But near its source at Immendingen, the riverbed is cracked limestone and the water drains into the ground; in 1921 that stretch was completely dry on 309 days. An 1877 salt and dye test found the water about 60 hours later at the Aach spring, roughly 12 km south, which flows into Lake Constance and the Rhine, and on to the North Sea. Geologists think the upper Danube may one day drain to the Rhine for good.

Imagery: NASA GIBS Blue Marble, Landsat WELD (NASA/USGS), AWS Terrain Tiles, Natural Earth. Cutaway animations are illustrative.

videos.title: Spain Has 5 Neighbours?! 🇪🇸🤯
videos.description:
Spain's neighbouring countries aren't just Portugal and France: Spain borders 5 countries, including Morocco in Africa, plus a Spanish town inside France and an island that changes country every 6 months.

Spain's land neighbours are Portugal, France, Andorra, the UK (through Gibraltar) and Morocco (around Ceuta, Melilla and the Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera). In 1934 a storm built a sand bar that joined the Peñón to the African coast, creating a border of about 85 metres. In 1659 Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees on Pheasant Island; the follow-up deal handed France 33 villages, but Llívia was a town, so it stayed Spanish and is now surrounded by France. Pheasant Island itself is shared: Spanish from 1 February to 31 July and French from 1 August to 31 January, an arrangement in force since 1902. Nobody lives there.

videos.title: Is Russia Bigger Than Pluto? 🇷🇺🤔
videos.description:
Is Russia bigger than Pluto? Russia covers about 17.1 million km², and for decades Pluto's whole surface was thought to be smaller. Then NASA's New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015 and measured it.

Through Hubble, Pluto looked about 2,300 km wide, which gives a surface of about 16.6 million km², so Russia won. In 2006 Pluto was voted out of the planet club. Then, after a 9.5-year trip, New Horizons measured Pluto at 2,377 km wide: a surface of about 17.7 million km². Pluto beats Russia by about 650,000 km², almost a whole Texas. And half of Pluto's famous heart, Sputnik Planitia, is named after Sputnik 1, the Soviet Union's first satellite.

videos.title: 6 Turkey Facts That Sound Fake 🇹🇷🤯
videos.description:
6 facts about Turkey (Türkiye) that sound fake: Istanbul on two continents, a whole sea inside one country, Santa Claus's real hometown, the Derinkuyu underground city and Göbekli Tepe.
Plus the twist: why a bird shares the country's name, and what Turks and Hindi speakers call it. COP31 is being held in Antalya, Turkey, from 9 to 20 November 2026.

About 97% of Turkey is in Asia, yet its biggest city, Istanbul, straddles the Bosphorus, and the capital is Ankara. The Sea of Marmara lies entirely inside Turkey and is often called the world's smallest sea. Saint Nicholas, who inspired Santa Claus, was bishop of Myra, today's Demre in Antalya province. The story goes that in 1963 a man renovating his house in Derinkuyu broke through a wall and found an underground city about 85 m deep, built for up to 20,000 people and their animals. Göbekli Tepe's stone pillars were raised about 11,500 years ago, roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge. The bird is called "turkey" in English after guineafowl traded through Ottoman lands; Turks call it "hindi" and Hindi calls it "peru". Since 2022 the UN uses "Türkiye".

Imagery: NASA GIBS (Blue Marble, Landsat WELD), AWS Terrain Tiles, Natural Earth. Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.

videos.title: Why SPACEX launches Rockets From Here? 🚀
videos.description:
Why does SpaceX launch Starship from Starbase, a lonely beach at the tip of Texas just a few km from Mexico? The answer is Earth's spin, the open Gulf to the east, and a plan to catch the ship with the tower's giant 'chopsticks'.

Earth turns east, and at Starbase's latitude (about 26°N) the ground moves at roughly 1,500 km/h, so a rocket launched east gets that speed for free. East of the pad lies over a thousand kilometres of open sea, so anything that goes wrong falls in the water, not on a city. Starbase also sits a little closer to the equator than Florida's Cape Canaveral. SpaceX has caught the Super Heavy booster before, but never the ship: on Flight 15 (targeted for 13 Nov 2026) the plan is for the ship to loop Earth about 14 times, re-enter over the Pacific, fly over northern Mexico and the Rio Grande Valley, cross the Gulf and turn back to the tower called Mechazilla. Plans and dates can change.

videos.title: NASA Found a Skull in Antarctica 💀
videos.description:
NASA's new satellite photo shows a skull on Vega Island, Antarctica, staring straight at Devil Island. Here's what made it, plus 4 more Antarctica facts that sound fake.

The "skull" is made of landforms: a rock peak (a nunatak) for the eye, a glacier moraine for the grin and Devil's Bay Glacier for the jaw. It stands out because a warm 2026 winter left little snow to cover the ice. Antarctica also holds Earth's coldest recorded temperature (−89.2 °C at Vostok Station, 1983), a liquid lake under about 4 km of ice, and ground about 3.5 km below sea level under the Denman Glacier. And on Vega Island itself, scientists found the skull of Vegavis, a bird about 69 million years old and an early relative of ducks.

videos.title: 6 Australia Facts That Can't Be Real 🇦🇺🤯
videos.description:
6 Australia facts that sound fake but are true: Australia is wider than the Moon, drifts 7 cm a year, imported camels, built the 5,614 km Dingo Fence and lost the Great Emu War of 1932.
Australia facts, the Emu War explained, and why the whole country moved 1.8 metres on the map.

Australia is almost 4,000 km wide; the Moon is about 3,474 km across. The continent drifts about 7 cm a year, so in 2017 its official coordinates moved 1.8 m. At least 15,000 camels arrived between 1870 and 1900, most from British India; when trucks took over they were set free, and today Australia has the world's biggest wild camel herd. The Dingo Fence runs 5,614 km. And in November 1932, about 20,000 emus raided Western Australian wheat farms: two machine guns and 10,000 rounds later, the soldiers went home.

videos.title: It Hasn't Rained Here in 2 Million Years?!
videos.description:
The McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica: why one of the driest places on Earth has almost no ice, and why NASA has tested Mars ideas here since the Viking missions.

The story goes, it hasn't rained here in about two million years. What's measured: mountains hold back the ice sheet, katabatic winds with gusts near 140 km/h scour the valleys, and the little snow that falls (around 10 cm a year) can turn straight to vapour within hours. Nothing rots: seals that wandered inland lie freeze-dried, some perhaps 2,000 years old. And microbes still live just under the surface of the rocks.

The 5 biggest countries in the world by area: Russia, Canada, the USA, China and Brazil.

Add lakes and coastal waters and the US moves ahead (about 9.8 vs 9.6). The gap is under 3%.

videos.title: Black Friday's Dark Secret! Police Hated Black Friday?! 🚓
videos.description:
Black Friday was named by the police, not by shops. In the 1950s, Philadelphia police used it for the chaotic day after Thanksgiving: traffic jams, crowds and shoplifters. Retailers hated it and in 1961 tried to rebrand it "Big Friday". Nobody listened. The original "Black Friday" was 24 September 1869, when two Wall Street speculators tried to corner the gold market and crashed it.

The name only spread nationally in the 1980s, and now Black Friday runs in well over a hundred countries that don't celebrate Thanksgiving, from the UK and Brazil to India, where it lands next to Diwali sales. Meanwhile China's Singles Day is bigger still: Alibaba alone sold about $38 billion in one day in 2019, more than US Black Friday and Cyber Monday online sales combined. This year, Black Friday is on 27 November.

videos.title: Britain Burns a Man Every Year?! 🤯
videos.description:
Every 5 November, Britain lights bonfires and burns a "guy" on top. The reason: in 1605, thirteen plotters hid 36 barrels of gunpowder under the House of Lords to blow up King James I. An anonymous letter gave them away, and on the night of 4 November guards found Guy Fawkes in the cellar with the matches.

Parliament made 5 November a compulsory day of thanksgiving by law (the Observance of 5th November Act 1606), which stayed in force for about 250 years until 1859. Fawkes himself was never burned: he jumped from the gallows and broke his neck. Today, Lewes in Sussex, a town of about 17,000, draws up to 80,000 people and carries 17 burning crosses, and the Yeomen of the Guard still search Parliament's cellars before every State Opening.

In Monaco, citizens aren't allowed into the gaming rooms of the famous Monte Carlo Casino. Monaco is only about 2 km², smaller than New York's Central Park, and about 39,000 people live there, but fewer than 1 in 4 are actual Monégasque citizens. Many moved in because there's no personal income tax.

The casino was built in the 1860s to save the principality's finances with visitors' money, not locals'. Monaco is also running out of room, so it builds land into the sea: its newest district, opened in 2024, added about 6 hectares worth around €1 billion. And its whole coastline is under 4 km.

videos.title: Canada Is South of Rome?! 🇨🇦
videos.description:
Canada's southernmost point, Middle Island in Lake Erie, sits at about 41.68° N. Rome is at about 41.9° N, so Canada's tip is further south than Rome, and even south of California's northern border (42° N). Toronto (about 43.65° N) is further south than Monaco (43.73° N), and in Windsor, Ontario, you drive north to reach Detroit in the USA.

So why does Canada feel so far north? Because Europe is further north than most people think: Paris is north of Montreal, London is north of Calgary. Europe stays milder thanks to the Gulf Stream, a warm ocean current from the Gulf of Mexico, while Canada gets the Arctic air.

videos.title: 5 Countries Fought Over a Lake?! 🌊
videos.description:
The world's biggest lake is called a sea. The Caspian covers about 370,000 km², bigger than Germany, and holds roughly 40% of all the lake water on Earth. It's salty, but only about a third as salty as the ocean, and its surface sits about 28 metres below sea level.

Five countries share it: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan. With oil and gas underneath, "sea or lake?" was worth billions: a sea is divided under maritime law, a lake between its shores. After more than 20 years of talks, the five signed a convention in 2018 that gave it a special status, neither fully a sea nor a lake. Meanwhile it's shrinking: in 2025 its level hit the lowest ever recorded.

videos.title: The Diwali Photo That Fooled India 🛰️
videos.description:
Every Diwali, a colourful "India from space on Diwali night" picture goes viral. It's not that. It's real satellite data, but not from Diwali and not from one night: a NOAA scientist made it in 2003 to show how India's city lights grew. Each colour is a year: white lights existed before 1992, blue appeared in 1992, green in 1998 and red in 2003.

What does real Diwali look like from space? NASA checked in 2012: the extra light was so subtle it's likely invisible from orbit. This year Diwali is on 8 November. When this photo shows up again, you'll know.

videos.title: Countries That Got Cheated on Coastline 🌊
videos.description:
Croatia's Pelješac Bridge project cost about €420 million (mostly EU-funded), just to avoid driving through 20 km of Bosnia. Some countries got the sea's leftovers: DR Congo, Africa's second-biggest country, has just 37 km of coastline. Iraq has over 430,000 km² of land and 58 km of coast. Jordan has 26 km on the Red Sea at Aqaba.

Bosnia and Herzegovina has about 20 km of coast and one seaside town, Neum, and that strip cuts Croatia in two. So Croatia built a 2.4 km bridge to go around it, opened in 2022. And the smallest coast of all? Monaco, about 4 km.

videos.title: Why France Borders Brazil 🤯
videos.description:
France's longest land border isn't with Spain. It's with Brazil. French Guiana, on the north coast of South America, isn't a colony: it's a full region of France and part of the European Union, so it uses the euro and EU rules on the edge of the Amazon. Its border with Brazil runs along the Oyapock River for about 650 to 730 km, depending on who measures, longer than the France–Spain border (about 623 km).

Europe launches its rockets from Kourou, about 500 km north of the equator, where Earth's spin gives rockets a free push. And the only bridge across the border was finished in 2011, but didn't open until March 2017. Six years, and nobody crossed.

videos.title: 40% of Canada is Almost Empty?! 🇨🇦
videos.description:
Canada has 10 provinces and 3 territories: Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut. Together the territories cover about 39% of Canada, more than all of India, yet only about 136,000 people live there, roughly 0.3% of Canadians, about one Narendra Modi Stadium.

Nunavut alone is about 2 million km², almost as big as Mexico, and its capital Iqaluit has no road to any other town. Provinces get their powers from Canada's constitution; territories get theirs from Ottawa through federal laws. The Northwest Territories and Nunavut have no political parties in their legislatures and govern by consensus, and in 2027 Nunavut takes control of its own land and resources.

videos.title: An Iceberg the Size of London?! 🧊
videos.description:
Iceberg A-81 broke off Antarctica's Brunt Ice Shelf, near the UK's Halley research station, in January 2023. At roughly 1,300–1,500 km², it is about the size of Greater London.

Over three years it drifted about 2,300 km through the Weddell Sea, past the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula and into the Scotia Sea, and in October 2026 it stalled off South Georgia. Ocean currents carry most Antarctic icebergs north through "iceberg alley" toward this island. A grounded giant can block penguins and seals from their feeding grounds (about half the world's southern elephant seals breed here), but as it melts it also releases nutrients that feed the ocean. A-68 (2020), A23a (2025), and now A-81: the third giant in six years.

videos.title: Chile to England… ON FOOT?! 🥾
videos.description:
In 1998, Karl Bushby set off from Punta Arenas, at the tip of Chile, with about 500 dollars and one rule: no motorised transport to move forward, and no going home until he walked there. He planned 10 to 12 years. It took 28.

He crossed the Darién Gap (and spent 18 days in a Panama jail), walked across the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia in 2006, was banned from Russia for five years, swam 288 km across the Caspian Sea in 2024, and swam the English Channel in October 2026, his first time on British soil since 1998. About 50,000 km and 29 countries later, he is due to finish in his hometown, Hull, on 2 November 2026.

videos.title: America Secretly uses Metric?! 🤯📏
videos.description:
Why doesn't the US use the metric system? Plot twist: since 1893 the US has officially defined its inch and pound using the metre and the kilogram, and today one inch is exactly 2.54 cm by definition.

Congress passed the Metric Conversion Act in 1975 but made it voluntary, and most people simply didn't switch. In 1999 one team's software gave thrust numbers in US units while NASA's navigation expected metric, and the Mars Climate Orbiter, part of a $327 million mission, flew too low and was lost. Until 2022 the US even had two different feet: the international foot and a slightly longer survey foot.

videos.title: Even F1 Cars Struggle Here?! 🇲🇽
videos.description:
Why do F1 cars struggle in Mexico City? The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez sits about 2,240 m up, the highest track on the calendar, and the air there is nearly a quarter thinner than at sea level.

Less air means less downforce, so teams bolt on Monaco-style maximum wings and still get roughly Monza-level grip. The turbo has to spin up to about 15% faster to feed the engine, and cooling the brakes and engine gets harder. But thin air also means less drag: in 2016 Valtteri Bottas hit 372.5 km/h here, the fastest speed recorded in an F1 race. This weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix runs on Sunday 1 November.

videos.title: 4 Indian States share same birthday?! 🇮🇳
videos.description:
Why do four Indian states share the same birthday? On 1 November 1956 the States Reorganisation Act redrew India's map on language lines.

videos.title: WHY DO STARS TWINKLE?!
videos.description:
Why do stars twinkle, and why don't planets? The twinkle isn't the star at all: it's about 100 km of moving air above your head.

Starlight from Sirius travels about 8.6 years to reach you, then gets bent around by warm and cold pockets of air in roughly its last third of a millisecond. Stars are so far away that their light arrives as a single point, so every pocket of air shoves it brighter, dimmer, left and right. Planets are much closer and show a tiny disc, so they usually shine steady. That's why astronomers climb: Chile's Atacama Desert hosts telescopes over 2,600 m up, India's Hanle observatory in Ladakh sits at about 4,500 m inside India's first dark sky reserve, Europe's new 39 m telescope will reshape a mirror about 1,000 times a second, and Hubble simply orbits about 480 km up, above the air.

Why is America colder than Europe? London is further north than all 48 mainland US states, yet New York is about 5°C colder in January. Is it really the Gulf Stream?

London sits at 51.5°N, north of every point in the mainland USA. In January it averages about +5°C; New York (40.7°N) is about 1°C, and Calgary, on London's latitude, about −8°C. videos.title: Earth Had 6 Kinds of Humans at Once 🤯 #geography #dna #neanderthal
videos.description:
How many human species lived on Earth at the same time? About 100,000 years ago there were six, and Neanderthal and Denisovan DNA is still in many people today.

Homo sapiens in Africa, Neanderthals in Europe, Denisovans in Siberia and East Asia, the last Homo erectus on Java, the one-metre "Hobbits" of Flores (Homo floresiensis) and Homo luzonensis in the Philippines, only named in 2019. By about 40,000 years ago the Neanderthals were gone, and one by one the others vanished. But our ancestors had children with them: people with roots in Europe or Asia carry about 1–2% Neanderthal DNA, and in Papua New Guinea it's up to about 5% Denisovan.

videos.title: Why Bengaluru Has 1,000s of Lakes but No River 🇮🇳
videos.description:
Why does Bengaluru have so many lakes when it has no big river? The history of Bengaluru's lakes, from 9th-century tanks to the Majestic bus stand.

Bengaluru sits on a ridge about 920 m up, with no major river nearby. So for more than 1,100 years, people built earth embankments across the valleys to trap monsoon rain, creating chains of tanks that overflow from one into the next: six cascading chains across three valleys. Kempegowda, who founded the city in 1537, kept building more. Then the city grew over them: from 1973 to 2013, about 79% of its water bodies vanished, and today water is pumped about 100 km from the Kaveri and lifted about 300 m. Some lost lakes are hiding in plain sight: Kanteerava Stadium (Sampangi Lake), KR Market (Siddikatte) and Majestic bus stand (Dharmambudhi).

videos.description:
Earth spins at a steady speed, so why do time zones look like they were drawn by a nervous squirrel? 🌍

Until 1883, every town set its clock by the Sun. Then American railroads reset their clocks on the "Day of Two Noons", and in 1884, 25 nations picked Greenwich as zero. But today's lines are drawn by governments: China runs one time zone across the whole country, France has 12, Samoa deleted a Friday in 2011, and Nepal sits 15 minutes ahead of India.

Why nobody put it out, why the town was moved instead, and how long the fire could keep burning.

The story goes, in 1962 the town burned its trash in an old mining pit and the fire reached the coal mines below. Flushing it ran out of money after about $42,000. A 1983 federal study put the cost of putting it out at $663 million; Congress gave $42 million to move people instead. About 500 homes and shops were torn down, and in 2002 even the ZIP code went. At its current rate, the fire could burn for another 250 years.

In the late 1950s, UFO sightings over America shot up. Decades later, the CIA said: "It was us."

The U-2 flew above 60,000 feet (about 18 km), while airliners of the time flew at 10,000–20,000 feet. At sunset its silver wings still caught the sunlight, so pilots far below reported fiery objects. SpaceX अपना Starship रॉकेट टेक्सस के कोने पर, मेक्सिको से बस कुछ किलोमीटर दूर, Starbase के एक सुनसान बीच से क्यों लॉन्च करता है? जवाब है धरती का घूमना, पूरब में खुला समुद्र, और टावर की बड़ी-सी 'चॉपस्टिक्स' से स्पेसशिप पकड़ने का प्लान।

धरती पूरब की ओर घूमती है, और Starbase (करीब 26°N) पर ज़मीन करीब 1,500 km/h से चलती है, तो पूरब में लॉन्च होने वाले रॉकेट को ये रफ़्तार मुफ़्त मिलती है। पूरब में 1,000 किलोमीटर से ज़्यादा खुला समुद्र है, तो कुछ गड़बड़ हो तो मलबा पानी में गिरता है, किसी शहर पर नहीं। Starbase फ्लोरिडा के Cape Canaveral से थोड़ा ज़्यादा इक्वेटर के पास भी है। SpaceX बूस्टर पहले पकड़ चुका है, शिप कभी नहीं: Flight 15 (13 नवंबर 2026 का लक्ष्य) में प्लान है कि शिप करीब 14 बार धरती का चक्कर लगाए, पैसिफ़िक के ऊपर से लौटे, उत्तरी मेक्सिको और रियो ग्रांडे के ऊपर से उड़कर, गल्फ़ पार करे और Mechazilla नाम के टावर पर वापस आए। प्लान और तारीख़ बदल सकती हैं।

मैप: NASA Blue Marble और Landsat, AWS Terrain Tiles, Natural Earth. दृश्य AI से बनाए गए चित्र हैं।

videos.title: NASA को Antarctica में मिली खोपड़ी 💀
videos.description:
NASA की नई satellite photo में Antarctica के Vega Island पर एक खोपड़ी (skull) दिखी है, जो Devil Island को घूर रही है। जानिए ये कैसे बनी, और अंटार्कटिका के 4 और फैक्ट्स जो झूठ लगते हैं।

ये "खोपड़ी" ज़मीन की बनावट से बनी है: आँख एक चट्टान (nunatak) है, मुस्कान glacier का मलबा (moraine), और जबड़ा Devil's Bay Glacier। 2026 की गर्म सर्दी में बर्फ़ कम गिरी, इसलिए ये साफ़ दिखी। अंटार्कटिका में धरती का सबसे कम तापमान (−89.2 °C, Vostok Station, 1983) दर्ज हुआ, करीब 4 किलोमीटर बर्फ़ के नीचे एक जमी नहीं हुई झील है, और Denman Glacier के नीचे ज़मीन sea level से करीब 3.5 किलोमीटर नीचे है। और Vega Island पर ही वैज्ञानिकों को Vegavis नाम के पक्षी की करीब 69 million साल पुरानी खोपड़ी मिली, जो बत्तखों का पुराना रिश्तेदार है।

Imagery: NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey. Globe: NASA Blue Marble (GIBS). Terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles. Borders: Natural Earth. Vegavis skull reconstruction: Joseph Groenke (Ohio University) and Christopher Torres (University of the Pacific).

videos.title: Australia के 6 फैक्ट्स जो सच नहीं लगते 🇦🇺🤯
videos.description:
ऑस्ट्रेलिया के 6 अजीब फैक्ट्स: Australia चाँद से भी चौड़ा है, हर साल 7 cm खिसकता है, ऊँट मँगवाए, 5,614 km लंबी Dingo Fence बनाई और 1932 में Emu War हार गया।
Australia facts in Hindi, Emu War की कहानी और क्यों पूरा देश नक्शे पर 1.8 metre खिसक गया।

Australia करीब 4,000 km चौड़ा है, चाँद करीब 3,474 km। महाद्वीप हर साल करीब 7 cm खिसकता है, इसलिए 2017 में उसके आधिकारिक coordinates 1.8 metre बदले गए। 1870 से 1900 के बीच कम से कम 15,000 ऊँट आए, ज़्यादातर British India से; ट्रक आने पर उन्हें छोड़ दिया गया और आज यहाँ दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा जंगली ऊँटों का झुंड है। Dingo Fence 5,614 km लंबी है। और November 1932 में करीब 20,000 emu गेहूँ के खेतों पर टूट पड़े: दो machine gun और 10,000 गोलियों के बाद फ़ौजी घर लौट गए।

videos.title: यहाँ 2 Million साल से बारिश नहीं?! 🇦🇶
videos.description:
अंटार्कटिका की McMurdo Dry Valleys: धरती की सबसे सूखी जगहों में से एक, जहाँ बर्फ़ लगभग नहीं है, और जहाँ NASA 1970s के Viking missions से Mars के ideas test करता रहा है।

कहते हैं यहाँ करीब 2 million साल से बारिश नहीं हुई। जो मापा गया है: पहाड़ ice sheet को रोकते हैं, करीब 140 km/h की katabatic हवाएँ घाटियों को सुखा देती हैं, और साल भर की थोड़ी snow (करीब 10 cm) कुछ घंटों में सीधे भाप बन सकती है। यहाँ कुछ सड़ता नहीं — भटककर आई seals सूखकर पड़ी हैं, कुछ शायद 2,000 साल पुरानी। और चट्टानों की सतह के ठीक नीचे microbes आज भी ज़िंदा हैं।

Map imagery: NASA GIBS (Blue Marble, MODIS), AWS Terrain Tiles. दृश्य AI से बनाए गए चित्र हैं।

videos.title: क्या Aliens ने बनाया? कोई नहीं समझा पाया! 😳👽🛸
videos.description:
चार प्राचीन जगहें जिन पर लोग आज भी बहस करते हैं। Peru की Nazca Lines: रेगिस्तान में 1,300 km से ज़्यादा लकीरें और विशाल आकृतियाँ, जिनमें 134 metre लंबा एक condor भी है। करीब 2,000 साल पुरानी, और सबसे अच्छी आसमान से दिखती हैं। Bolivia का Puma Punku: पत्थर इतनी सटीकता से कटे कि आपस में बदले जा सकें, Andes में करीब 3,850 metre की ऊँचाई पर।

Lebanon का Baalbek: मंदिर के पत्थर करीब 800 tonnes के, और खदान में करीब 1,650 tonnes का एक block, अब तक का सबसे बड़ा कटा पत्थर। और Egypt का Great Pyramid: करीब 2.3 million blocks, लगभग एकदम true north की सीध में, और करीब 3,800 साल तक धरती की सबसे ऊँची इमारत। Aliens, या प्राचीन लोग जो हमारी सोच से कहीं ज़्यादा smart थे? आप तय करिए।

videos.title: Britain हर साल एक आदमी को जलाता है?! 🤯
videos.description:
हर 5 November को Britain में bonfires जलते हैं और सबसे ऊपर एक "guy" का पुतला जलाया जाता है। वजह: 1605 में 13 साज़िशकर्ताओं ने King James I को उड़ाने के लिए House of Lords के नीचे gunpowder के 36 barrels छिपाए थे। एक गुमनाम चिट्ठी ने राज़ खोल दिया, और 4 November की रात guards ने Guy Fawkes को cellar में माचिस के साथ पकड़ लिया।

Parliament ने 5 November को कानूनन शुक्राना मनाने का दिन बना दिया (Observance of 5th November Act 1606), जो करीब 250 साल, 1859 तक लागू रहा। Fawkes खुद कभी नहीं जला: वो फाँसी के तख्ते से कूदा और उसकी गर्दन टूट गई। आज Sussex का कस्बा Lewes, जहाँ करीब 17,000 लोग रहते हैं, bonfire night पर 80,000 तक लोगों को खींचता है और 17 जलते crosses निकालता है। और Parliament के हर State Opening से पहले Yeomen of the Guard आज भी cellars की तलाशी लेते हैं।

Imagery: NASA GIBS Blue Marble / Landsat, Natural Earth. Scenes are AI-generated illustrations.

videos.title: Canada का 40% लगभग खाली?! 🍁
videos.description:
Canada में 10 provinces और 3 territories हैं: Yukon, Northwest Territories और Nunavut। तीनों मिलकर Canada का करीब 39% हैं, पूरे भारत से भी बड़े, पर वहाँ सिर्फ़ करीब 1,36,000 लोग रहते हैं, यानी Canada के लोगों का 0.3%, लगभग एक Narendra Modi Stadium भर।

अकेला Nunavut करीब 20 लाख km² है, लगभग Mexico जितना, और उसकी राजधानी Iqaluit तक किसी दूसरे शहर से कोई सड़क नहीं जाती। Provinces को ताकत Canada के संविधान से मिलती है; territories को Ottawa के federal laws से। Northwest Territories और Nunavut की विधानसभाओं में कोई political party नहीं, वहाँ सहमति से सरकार चलती है, और 2027 में Nunavut अपनी ज़मीन और संसाधनों का नियंत्रण खुद लेगा।

videos.title: London जितना बड़ा iceberg?! 🧊
videos.description:
Iceberg A-81 January 2023 में Antarctica की Brunt Ice Shelf से टूटा, UK के Halley research station के पास। करीब 1,300–1,500 km² का ये iceberg लगभग Greater London जितना बड़ा है।

तीन साल में ये Weddell Sea से होकर, Antarctic Peninsula के छोर के पास से, Scotia Sea तक करीब 2,300 km बहा, और October 2026 में South Georgia के पास अटक गया। समुद्री धाराएँ ज़्यादातर Antarctic icebergs को "iceberg alley" से इसी द्वीप की तरफ़ ले जाती हैं। अटका हुआ विशाल iceberg penguins और seals का खाने तक का रास्ता रोक सकता है, पर पिघलते हुए ये समुद्र को पोषक तत्व भी देता है। A-68 (2020), A23a (2025) और अब A-81: छह साल में तीसरा।

videos.title: Chile से England… पैदल?! 🥾
videos.description:
1998 में Karl Bushby, Chile के आख़िरी छोर Punta Arenas से करीब 500 dollar और एक नियम के साथ निकले: आगे बढ़ने के लिए कोई गाड़ी नहीं, और पैदल पहुँचे बिना घर नहीं लौटना। सोचा था 10 से 12 साल। लगे 28।

उन्होंने Darién Gap पार किया (और Panama की jail में 18 दिन बिताए), 2006 में जमे हुए Bering Strait पर Alaska से Russia पैदल गए, Russia में 5 साल का ban झेला, 2024 में Caspian Sea में 288 km तैरे, और October 2026 में English Channel तैरकर 1998 के बाद पहली बार British ज़मीन पर कदम रखा। करीब 50,000 km और 29 देशों के बाद, उन्हें 2 November 2026 को अपने शहर Hull पहुँचना है।

videos.title: अमेरिका चुपके से metric चलाता है?! 🤯📏
videos.description:
अमेरिका metric system क्यों नहीं अपनाता? Twist ये है: 1893 से अमेरिका अपना inch और pound, metre और kilogram से तय करता है, और आज एक inch परिभाषा से ठीक 2.54 cm है।

1975 में Congress ने Metric Conversion Act पास किया, पर उसे मर्ज़ी पर छोड़ दिया, और ज़्यादातर लोगों ने switch ही नहीं किया। 1999 में एक team के software ने numbers US units में दिए जबकि NASA की navigation metric मान रही थी, और Mars Climate Orbiter ($327 million का mission) बहुत नीचे से गुज़रा और खो गया। 2022 तक अमेरिका में दो अलग foot भी चलते थे: international foot और थोड़ा लंबा survey foot।

Imagery: NASA GIBS Blue Marble / Landsat, AWS Terrain Tiles, Natural Earth. दृश्य AI से बनाए गए चित्र हैं।

videos.title: 4 राज्यों का एक ही birthday?! 🇮🇳
videos.description:
भारत के चार राज्यों का birthday एक ही दिन क्यों है? 1 November 1956 को States Reorganisation Act ने भाषा के आधार पर भारत का नक्शा दोबारा बनाया।

उससे पहले भारत 29 इकाइयों का जोड़-तोड़ था, जो Part A, B, C और D में बँटी थीं। 1952 में Potti Sreeramulu ने तेलुगु बोलने वालों के अलग राज्य के लिए अनशन किया; 58वें दिन उनकी मौत हो गई, और तीन दिन बाद नेहरू ने आंध्र का ऐलान किया। फिर फ़ज़ल अली आयोग ने नक्शा दोबारा बनाया, और 1 November 1956 को 29 इकाइयाँ 14 राज्य और 6 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश बन गईं। उस दिन जन्मे: केरल, आंध्र प्रदेश, मध्य प्रदेश (तब सबसे बड़ा राज्य) और Mysore State, जो 1973 में कर्नाटक बना। इस साल केरल 70 का हो गया, नए आधिकारिक नाम केरलम के साथ।

videos.title: Diwali की वो फोटो जिसने India को ठगा 🛰️
videos.description:
हर Diwali "Diwali की रात space से भारत" वाली एक रंगीन फोटो viral होती है। वो ऐसा नहीं है। ये असली satellite data है, पर Diwali का नहीं और एक रात का भी नहीं: NOAA के एक वैज्ञानिक ने इसे 2003 में बनाया था, ये दिखाने के लिए कि भारत के शहरों की रोशनी कैसे बढ़ी। हर रंग एक साल है: सफ़ेद रोशनी 1992 से पहले की, नीली 1992, हरी 1998 और लाल 2003।

videos.title: भारत ने अपना GPS क्यों बनाया? 🇮🇳
videos.description:
भारत का अपना GPS — NavIC — क्या है और ये क्यों ज़रूरी है? 30 October 2026 को NVS-03 launch के साथ NavIC को चौथा satellite मिला।

आपके फ़ोन को 3D में जगह तय करने के लिए कम से कम चार satellites चाहिए। NavIC पूरे भारत और सीमा के पार करीब 1,500 km तक कवर करता है, पर पुरानी atomic clocks खराब होने और 2025 में NVS-02 के गलत orbit में अटकने के बाद, खबरों के मुताबिक सिर्फ़ तीन चल रहे थे। ISRO के GSLV-F18 ने 2,232 kg का NVS-03, भारत में बनी atomic clock के साथ, सही orbit में पहुँचाया।

videos.title: एक और धरती है?!
videos.description:
धरती का सबसे पास वाला जुड़वाँ ग्रह Proxima b सिर्फ़ 4.2 light-years दूर है। तो हम वहाँ जा क्यों नहीं सकते? Nearest Earth-like planet (सबसे नज़दीकी धरती जैसा ग्रह) 60 सेकंड में।

Proxima b एक पथरीला ग्रह है, कम से कम धरती जितना भारी, जो सूरज के सबसे पास वाले तारे Proxima Centauri के habitable zone में घूमता है। रोशनी को भी वहाँ पहुँचने में 4.2 साल लगते हैं; Voyager 1 को करीब 60,000 km/h की रफ़्तार से लगभग 76,000 साल लगेंगे। वहाँ एक साल सिर्फ़ 11.2 दिन का है, और ये अपने तारे के धरती-सूरज की दूरी से करीब 20 गुना पास है, इसलिए शायद इसका एक हिस्सा हमेशा तारे की ओर रहता है। मई 2019 में इसका तारा कुछ सेकंड में ultraviolet में करीब 14,000 गुना तेज़ चमका। वहाँ हवा है या नहीं, अभी पता नहीं।

तारे क्यों टिमटिमाते हैं (tare kyu timtimate hai)? असल में तारा नहीं, हमारे ऊपर करीब 100 km हवा टिमटिमाती है।

Sirius की रोशनी करीब 8.6 साल चलकर आती है, और आख़िरी एक millisecond से भी कम में गरम-ठंडी हवा उसे इधर-उधर मोड़ देती है। तारे इतने दूर हैं कि उनकी रोशनी एक बिंदु बनकर आती है, इसलिए हवा उसे तेज़-धीमा और दाएँ-बाएँ धकेलती है। ग्रह पास हैं और छोटी थाली जैसे दिखते हैं, इसलिए आमतौर पर स्थिर चमकते हैं। इसीलिए टेलिस्कोप ऊँचाई पर लगते हैं: चिली के Atacama में 2,600 m से ऊपर, और लद्दाख के हानले में करीब 4,500 m, जो भारत का पहला dark sky reserve है। यूरोप का नया 39 m टेलिस्कोप अपना शीशा सेकंड में करीब 1,000 बार मोड़ेगा, और Hubble करीब 480 km ऊपर हवा से बाहर घूमता है।

videos.title: अमेरिका लंदन से ज़्यादा ठंडा क्यों है? 🥶
videos.description:
अमेरिका यूरोप से ज़्यादा ठंडा क्यों है? लंदन, अमेरिका के 48 मेनलैंड स्टेट्स से भी ज़्यादा उत्तर में है, फिर भी जनवरी में न्यूयॉर्क करीब 5°C ज़्यादा ठंडा रहता है। क्या वजह सच में Gulf Stream (गल्फ़ स्ट्रीम) है?
Gulf Stream मदद करती है, पर असली वजहें हैं हवा और रॉकी पहाड़।

लंदन 51.5°N पर है, मेनलैंड अमेरिका के हर हिस्से से ऊपर। जनवरी में लंदन का औसत करीब +5°C, न्यूयॉर्क (40.7°N) करीब 1°C, और लंदन की ही लाइन पर कैलगरी करीब −8°C। 2002 में कोलंबिया यूनिवर्सिटी के वैज्ञानिकों ने क्लाइमेट मॉडल से जाँचा: समुद्र की गर्मी यूरोप को बस कुछ डिग्री गर्म करती है, और अटलांटिक के दोनों तरफ़ लगभग बराबर। बाकी फ़र्क पश्चिमी हवाओं (यूरोप की हवा समुद्र पार करके आती है, न्यूयॉर्क की जमे हुए महाद्वीप से) और रॉकी पहाड़ों से मुड़ी जेट स्ट्रीम का है। सटीक हिस्सेदारी पर वैज्ञानिकों में अब भी बहस है।
